title: Two Sum IV - Input is a BST
statement: You get `root`, the root of a binary search tree (each node's left subtree holds only smaller values and its right subtree only larger ones, so no value repeats), and an integer `k`. Decide whether two different nodes of the tree have values that add up to exactly `k`: return `true` if such a pair exists and `false` if not. A single node cannot be used twice.
constraints: root is a valid binary search tree
notes:
## Intuition

This is Two Sum on a tree. While walking the tree, keep a set of the values already visited: a node with value `v` completes a pair exactly when `k - v` was seen earlier. Each pair is found when its second node is visited, so one traversal is enough. The brute force collects all values and tries every pair, which is O(n²).

## Approach

1. Create an empty set `seen`.
2. `dfs(node)`: an empty subtree finds nothing, so return `false`.
3. If `k - node.val` is in `seen`, some earlier node pairs with this one: return `true`.
4. Otherwise add `node.val` to `seen` and search the left subtree, then the right one, stopping as soon as either finds a pair.
5. Return `dfs(root)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`k = 9`. The walk visits 5 first: it needs 4, `seen` is empty, so add 5. At 3 it needs 6, which is missing; add 3. At 2 it needs 7, missing; add 2. Node 2 has no children, so the walk returns to node 4, which needs `9 - 4 = 5`. 5 is in `seen`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is visited at most once, with O(1) set operations.
- Space: O(n) for `seen` plus O(h) for the recursion, where h is the tree's height.

## Pitfalls

- Look up `k - node.val` before adding `node.val`; otherwise `k = 2 · node.val` would wrongly pair a node with itself.
- Values may be negative, and so may `k`; do not prune by assuming positive numbers.
- Stop as soon as a pair is found: `dfs(node.left) || dfs(node.right)` skips the right subtree when the left one already succeeds.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | values of the nodes visited so far |
| `dfs` | searches one subtree, returning whether a pair has been completed |
| `node` | the node being visited |
